validity.recommendation: Leave Diameter UNRESOLVED for P6830 (line I) -- do not fill it from P6831's sourced 530 mm, and do not fabricate a 1020 mm value off an unverifiable lead. Re-open only if a source for line I's own diameter surfaces (e.g. a Wayback capture of kaztag.kz, or the AlatauGorProekt/Intergas design file).
validity.researcher_notes: This confirms and extends cluster G's own verdict (staged in batches/kazakhstan-gas/staging/redundancy/staged_resolutions.json) that line I's diameter has no public source -- I independently re-hunted and reached the same dead end. Two Kazakh business-press pieces (kapital.kz/economic/34300/vveden-gazoprovod-almaty-bayserke-talgar.html, verified live, '64,4' present; agrs.kz/novosti/otkrytie-gazoprovoda-almaty-bajserke-talgar.html, verified live) independently corroborate line I's length (64.4 km), capacity (2.4 bcm/y) and 2014 launch, but NEITHER states a diameter. One lead that did NOT pan out: a web search summary attributed 'diameter 1020 and 530 mm' to a kaztag.kz article on this pipeline (headline 'Магистральный газопровод Алматы-Байсерке-Талгар введен в эксплуатацию'), which -- if real and if the two figures split by line -- would read as line I=1020mm/line II=530mm. I could not confirm this: kaztag.kz returns HTTP 403 both via curl (browser UA) and scripts/url_verifier.py, it has no Wayback snapshot (CDX query empty), and neither tengrinews.kz nor the Forbes.kz republication of the same wire story (both fetched directly) mention any diameter figure at all. Per the no-fabrication rule this is documented as a chased-and-failed lead, not cited. Separately, cluster G's own open item (P6831's 8.80 bcm/y looking implausible for a 530mm/62km line) is resolved as a side-finding, not by me for this row: intergas.kz/ru/news/4/1040 and neftegazpro.ru both independently give line II's capacity as '1 000 000 m3/hour', which annualizes to ~8.76 bcm/y -- consistent with the sheet's 8.80, so that figure is plausible, not an error (worth noting on P6831's own shard).
